title: "Tool 2 — The CKA Penalty"
subtitle: "Close the hole · sweep μ · read the frontier"

*Learn-the-tool track · Lab 2 of 3.*

The hero rung.  `fair_fit` minimizes $\text{loss} = \text{fit} +
\mu\,\operatorname{Dep}(\hat y, S)$ with a kernel dependence penalty.  You will
close the nonlinear hole, then sweep $\mu$ to trace the trade-off frontier.

---

## 1 · Close the Hole

::: {#88defd9e .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
d = datasets.fair_regression(n=1000, seed=0)
x, S, y = d["x"], d["s"], d["y"]

y0 = fair_fit(x, y, S, mu=0.0)
y8 = fair_fit(x, y, S, mu=8.0)

print(f"plain (μ=0):   CKA={cka_rbf(y0, S):.3f}")
print(f"CKA penalty:   CKA={cka_rbf(y8, S):.3f}   ← curve gone")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
plain (μ=0):   CKA=0.284
CKA penalty:   CKA=0.019   ← curve gone
```
:::
:::

## 2 · Sweep Μ — The Frontier

::: {#174ea8cb .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
sweep = [0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0, 8.0, 20.0]
print(f"{'μ':>6}  {'accuracy':>9}  {'CKA(ŷ,S)':>9}")
print("-" * 28)
acc, dep = [], []
for mu in sweep:
    p = fair_fit(x, y, S, mu=mu)
    a = max(1 - np.mean((p - y) ** 2) / np.var(y), 0.0)
    c = cka_rbf(p, S)
    acc.append(a); dep.append(c)
    print(f"{mu:>6g}  {a:>9.3f}  {c:>9.3f}")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
     μ   accuracy   CKA(ŷ,S)
----------------------------
     0      0.952      0.284
   0.5      0.879      0.198
     1      0.782      0.147
     2      0.642      0.090
     5      0.453      0.034
     8      0.378      0.019
    20      0.285      0.007
```
:::
:::


::: {#cell-fig-tool2-frontier .cell execution_count=5}
``` {.python .cell-code}
dep_arr, acc_arr = np.array(dep), np.array(acc)

# the elbow: the sweep point farthest from the chord joining the two endpoints
dep_unit = (dep_arr - dep_arr.min()) / (np.ptp(dep_arr) + 1e-9)
acc_unit = (acc_arr - acc_arr.min()) / (np.ptp(acc_arr) + 1e-9)
start = np.array([dep_unit[0], acc_unit[0]])
chord = np.array([dep_unit[-1] - dep_unit[0], acc_unit[-1] - acc_unit[0]])
chord = chord / np.linalg.norm(chord)
offsets = np.column_stack([dep_unit, acc_unit]) - start
dist = np.linalg.norm(offsets - (offsets @ chord)[:, None] * chord, axis=1)
knee = int(np.argmax(dist))
print(f"elbow at μ = {sweep[knee]:g}  (CKA {dep_arr[knee]:.2f}, R² {acc_arr[knee]:.2f})")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 4.4))
ax.plot(dep_arr, acc_arr, "-o", c=COOL, lw=2.2)
for mu, dx, ay in zip(sweep, dep_arr, acc_arr):
    ax.annotate(f"μ={mu:g}", (dx, ay), textcoords="offset points",
                xytext=(6, 6), fontsize=9, color=INK)
ax.scatter([dep_arr[knee]], [acc_arr[knee]], s=240, facecolors="none",
           edgecolors=CRASH, lw=2.6, zorder=5)
ax.set_xlabel("CKA(ŷ, S)  →  less neutral"); ax.set_ylabel("accuracy (R²)")
ax.set_title("The accuracy–neutrality frontier", fontsize=12)
despine(ax)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
elbow at μ = 1  (CKA 0.15, R² 0.78)
```
:::

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![Accuracy vs neutrality, elbow circled. Right of the elbow, neutrality is nearly free; left of it, every further drop in CKA costs real accuracy.](lab-tool2-cka-penalty_files/figure-html/fig-tool2-frontier-output-2.png){#fig-tool2-frontier width=880 height=514}
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## What to Look for
There is no single "fair model" — there is a curve.  Pick the smallest $\mu$
that pushes CKA below your threshold; everything to its right buys neutrality you
may not need at an accuracy cost you do pay.
:::

---

## 3 · The Real Thing — `keras-fairkl`

`fair_fit` is the closed-form teaching stand-in.  The production version
trains the penalty **end to end**: `FairModelWrapper` adds $\mu \cdot
\operatorname{CKA}(\hat y, S)$ to whatever task loss you compile, and the
sensitive attribute rides in at `fit` time only — never as a model input.

::: {#51584683 .cell execution_count=6}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import os
os.environ["KERAS_BACKEND"] = "jax"
import keras
from keras import layers
from fairkl import FairModelWrapper

X_in = np.column_stack([x, S])     # the net SEES S — the penalty polices it

for mu in (0.0, 4.0):
    keras.utils.set_random_seed(0)
    mlp = keras.Sequential([layers.Dense(32, activation="tanh"),
                            layers.Dense(32, activation="tanh"),
                            layers.Dense(1)])
    model = FairModelWrapper(mlp, mu=mu)     # loss = mse + μ·CKA(ŷ, S)
    model.compile(optimizer=keras.optimizers.Adam(0.01), loss="mse")
    model.fit(X_in, y[:, None], q=S[:, None],
              epochs=400, batch_size=len(x), verbose=0)
    pred = model.predict(X_in, verbose=0)[:, 0]
    r2 = max(1 - np.mean((pred - y) ** 2) / np.var(y), 0.0)
    print(f"μ={mu:g}:  CKA(ŷ,S) = {cka_rbf(pred, S):.3f}   R² = {r2:.3f}")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
μ=0:  CKA(ŷ,S) = 0.280   R² = 0.950
μ=4:  CKA(ŷ,S) = 0.063   R² = 0.739
```
:::
:::


Same frontier, real optimizer, any architecture — this is the API the
[credit job](lab-jobB-neutralize-credit.qmd) scales to real data.
